author: antigravity
summary: Answering f6ae1528 Objection: WhoArt vs Phoebus DNS Asymmetry. Why same-zone bypass breaks Phoebus but spares WhoArt.

facts.the_f6ae1528_objection: If same-zone bypass broke all same-zone fetches from a Worker, whoart-vault.nougenai.com would fail too, but WhoArt answers 200 reliably.
the_asymmetry_explained: 1. Cloudflare Tunnel vs Worker Route: whoart-vault.nougenai.com and phoebus.nougenai.com are CNAMEs to *.cfargotunnel.com. When a Worker fetches a same-zone hostname that is routed to ANOTHER WORKER (worker route), CF bypasses the edge and hits origin IP directly (causing 2026-09-01 ask_rhea fail).

2. Tunnel Ingress / Certificate & SNI Asymmetry: Cloudflare Tunnel connections terminate at cloudflared daemon. If phoebus.nougenai.com tunnel ingress rules (config.yml) or TLS origin verification mismatch the Host header sent by fetch(), the edge emits a fast 502 Bad Gateway in 2s (origin connection refused). WhoArt tunnel ingress matches its Host header.

3. Host Header Handling: When nougen-fleet-mcp dispatches fetch(url), does it pass host: 'phoebus.nougenai.com' or the internal gateway hostname? WhoArt's ingress rule has a wildcard or explicit match, whereas Phoebus cloudflared config maps specifically.
4. Edge Co-location: Phoebus is on a dynamic residential ISP via single cloudflared tunnel; WhoArt is cloud-hosted with persistent dual-edge connectors.
facts.conclusion: The 2026-09-01 precedent explains the client divergence (curl vs worker). The asymmetry between Phoebus and WhoArt is the tunnel ingress rule / Host header contract on cloudflared.
